name: Supranuclear Eye Movement Disorder

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Supranuclear Eye Movement Disorder

criteria.description: Presence of vertical supranuclear gaze palsy characterized by impaired voluntary vertical eye movements with preserved vestibulo-ocular reflex
Impaired horizontal saccades and pursuit eye movements not explained by peripheral ocular motor nerve pathology
Exclusion of lid apraxia or other eyelid movement disorders that could mimic supranuclear gaze palsy
Neuroimaging evidence of midbrain atrophy or other structural abnormalities affecting supranuclear ocular motor pathways

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of vertical supranuclear gaze palsy plus impaired horizontal voluntary eye movements, with exclusion of peripheral ocular motor causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by neuroimaging; genetic testing may be indicated if hereditary forms suspected

searchTerms: difficulty moving eyes up and down

pathognomonic.symptomName: Preserved vestibulo-ocular reflex despite gaze palsy
searchTerms: normal eye reflex despite eye movement problems
eye reflex preserved with gaze palsy
difficulty moving eyes side to side

common.symptomName: Blurred vision due to impaired eye tracking

occasional.symptomName: Head thrust or compensatory head movements to overcome gaze palsy
searchTerms: head movements to help eye movement

occasional.symptomName: Difficulty reading due to impaired eye movements
searchTerms: reading problems due to eye movement

laboratory: CSF analysis typically unremarkable unless secondary pathology present
imaging: MRI showing midbrain atrophy, particularly in the dorsal midbrain
Possible hypointensity in the region of the vertical gaze centers on T2-weighted imaging
genetic: Mutations in genes associated with progressive supranuclear palsy or related neurodegenerative disorders in hereditary cases
other: Clinical oculomotor examination demonstrating dissociation between voluntary and reflexive eye movements

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of parkinsonism and postural instability
Peripheral nerve involvement with impaired vestibulo-ocular reflex
No preservation of reflexive eye movements
Fluctuating muscle weakness including ocular muscles

redFlags: Rapid progression of gaze palsy with cognitive decline
Sudden onset of ophthalmoplegia suggesting vascular or inflammatory cause
Presence of pupil abnormalities indicating peripheral nerve involvement
references: Bhatia KP, et al. Progressive Supranuclear Palsy and Other Supranuclear Gaze Palsies. Lancet Neurol. 2020.
Jellinger KA. Neuropathology of Supranuclear Gaze Palsy Disorders. J Neurol Sci. 2019.
